findings.what: The rewritten U1 test is still titled 'parity: ... carries its reference's components', but it no longer reads a reference. It checks behaviour on the design fixture.
findings.why: web-testing: only a test labelled 'reachable:' or 'parity:' may pass at the stub, and the design fixture is for parity only, never for behaviour. The test now checks the N4 acceptance line (David's A1 ruling), so its title and fixture misdescribe it. A behaviour check is sitting under a parity exemption.

findings.what: The test pins the builder's exact Matrix.tsx sentence, copied in after green ('The matrix counts a rule's tests at the node that built it, while ...').
findings.why: Anti-oracle: no test is edited to match the code. The ruling asked the test to assert N4's line (the note drawn from per-node counts, with no not-built-yet marker), not the implementation's prose. The rule, node and count assertions already prove the behaviour. The verbatim sentence only fixes the wording.

findings.what: Commit 4c59afec is trailered 'TDD: red' and fixes A1/I1, but its gate.finding-red exited 0. Per the receipt it was a test rewrite, 'not fail-first'.
findings.why: requirements-trace: a test written from a finding fails before the fix commit and passes after it. David's ruling authorises the rewrite, but the red trailer tells the trail it was red when it never was. The trail should record it as a ruled rewrite, not as red.
